title: Certificates of Deposit: which account receives repointed interest
content:
## Scope

This rule applies when a Certificates of Deposit certificate's interest is being paid out to checking or to savings and the payout account it names has been closed. It identifies the account that becomes the payout account on record.

## Rule

1. **Same kind first.** The payout account on record becomes the owner's active account of the same kind as the disposition pays to: an active checking account for pay to checking, and an active savings account for pay to savings.
2. **As the records stand.** The replacement account is the owner's active account of that kind as it stands in the bank's records when the change is recorded.
3. **No account of that kind.** When the owner holds no active account of that kind, the disposition becomes compound, and the payout account is the owner's active account of the other kind.

## Decision table

| Disposition paying to the closed account | Owner has an active account of the same kind? | Payout account on record becomes | Disposition afterwards |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pay to checking | Yes | The owner's active checking account | Pay to checking |
| Pay to checking | No | The owner's active savings account | Compound |
| Pay to savings | Yes | The owner's active savings account | Pay to savings |
| Pay to savings | No | The owner's active checking account | Compound |

## Cases (hypothetical owners)

- Interest paid to savings; that savings account closed; the owner has another savings account, active: interest now goes to that active savings account.
- Interest paid to checking; that checking account closed; the owner has no active checking account but has an active savings account: the disposition becomes compound, and the active savings account is recorded as the payout account.

## Points of judgement

**Does the owner pick the replacement from any account they like?**
The replacement is the owner's active account of the kind the disposition pays to, as it stands in the bank's records when the change is recorded.
